title: Copilot Studio: block maker-provided credentials for tool authentication
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, credential restriction, licensing statements and control paths are supported. The Dataverse reference documents the update operation and its writable credential-blocking property; the sharing control remains distinct from the runtime restriction.

claims.claim: Control maker credential options lets administrators restrict how makers authenticate agent tools.
claims.quote: The Control maker credential options feature enables this by letting you control how a maker can authenticate tools in an agent.

claims.claim: Authenticated tools such as connectors or Power Automate flows can use a maker's personal credentials.
claims.quote: a maker could add a tool that requires authentication to another service (like a connector or Power Automate flow) using their personal credentials.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A tool configured with maker credentials authenticates to connected services as the maker rather than the end user.
claims.quote: When someone uses the agent, the agent uses the maker's credentials, not the end user's credentials, to authenticate with connected services.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Microsoft's example of oversharing is an end user retrieving information or performing actions permitted only to the maker.
claims.quote: an end user might retrieve information or perform actions that only the maker's account is permitted to do.

claims.claim: Enforcing end-user credentials limits actions to what the end user's own account permits.
claims.quote: The action runs under the end-user's identity. If the user lacks permission for something, the agent is unable to do it on their behalf - by design.

claims.claim: Administrators can allow end-user credentials, maker-provided credentials, or both.
claims.quote: You choose whether makers can select to use their own credentials for authenticating tool connections, to use the end-user's credentials, or to have access to both.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in: by default both End-user and Maker-provided credentials remain enabled.
claims.quote: By default, both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The documented restriction immediately removes the maker's ability to select maker credentials.
claims.quote: the feature immediately turns off the maker's ability to select their credentials for authenticating tools within the environment or environment group.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: All tools for all agents in affected environments change to require end-user credentials at runtime.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users in new affected conversations are prompted to sign in to the connected service when needed.
claims.quote: Enforcing the use of end-user credentials prompts the end user to sign in (to the relevant service or connector) when needed.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center credential-control route is Manage > Environments (or Environment groups) > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options.
claims.quote: select Manage. Select Environments or Environment groups. ... select Settings ... Expand the Product section, and select Features. ... Copilot Studio agents ... Under Control maker credential options

claims.claim: PATCH /organizations(<organizationid>) updates the Dataverse organization record.
claims.quote: Update Event: True | PATCH /organizations(organizationid) See Update

claims.claim: The update request can set the writable Boolean blockcopilotauthorauthentication to true to prevent maker credential reuse.
claims.quote: Prevent makers from allowing end-users to use their credentials during authentication to use connectors, actions, flows, and triggers that are connected to an agent; LogicalName: blockcopilotauthorauthentication; Type: Boolean; True Label: Yes

claims.claim: Environment Admin is the documented UI role for configuring a single environment.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin permissions (Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups).

claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator or Global Admin is the documented UI role for environment groups.
claims.quote: Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups

claims.claim: Configuring an environment in a group requires a tenant administrator with access to that group.
claims.quote: If the environment you want to configure is part of an environment group, you must be a tenant admin with access to the group.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: For grouped environments the options are unavailable individually and administrators must configure the group's details page.
claims.quote: You can't configure this feature on the individual details page for environments that are in a group, you must use the group's details page.

claims.claim: Environment group credential-policy settings override individual environment settings.
claims.quote: you can't individually disable it for one environment in that group - environment group settings override any environment settings.

claims.claim: No stored maker credentials are used at runtime when end-user credentials are enforced.
claims.quote: No stored maker credentials are used at run time, aligning the agent's behavior with the end user's actual permissions.

claims.claim: Learn documents no additional credential type remaining available under this maker-credential restriction.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio block maker provided credentials exception service principal managed identity authentication. Read configure-no-maker-authentication and configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials; system identities are described for sharing, not as exceptions to this restriction.

claims.claim: Under this restriction each tool call needs authentication with a live user sign-in.
claims.quote: agents require real-time user interaction because each tool call must be authenticated with a live user sign-in.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Scheduled, autonomously triggered and background agents fail due to missing credentials when maker credentials are blocked.
claims.quote: agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials.

claims.claim: All agent triggers must involve an active user under the credential restriction.
claims.quote: All agent triggers must involve an active user.

claims.claim: The configured rule applies to existing and new agents in the selected environment or environment group.
claims.quote: Once active, all existing and new agents in that environment adhere to this rule ... The policy is applied per environment (or environment group).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Makers whose tools used their own credentials might be prompted to change the configuration before publishing.
claims.quote: If the maker previously had a tool configured with their credentials, they might be prompted to change it before publishing the agent.

claims.claim: The credential control covers connectors, built-in actions and embedded Power Automate flows equally.
claims.quote: The control over the authentication type covers connectors, built-in actions, and embedded Power Automate flows equally.

claims.claim: A Power Automate flow used as a tool requires each user to sign in for the connections it uses.
claims.quote: A Power Automate flow as a tool in the agent also requires each user to sign in for any connections that flow uses.

claims.claim: The update might take a minute to propagate.
claims.quote: The update might take a minute to propagate.
